status: measured workers-rs 0.8.7 glue and stack inputs (local workerd 2026-10-23, round2 run probe1); the probe is a measurement tool, so its JS reserve stays unmeasured and the build uses the unmeasured-model feature. The coordinator's model takes these glue inputs at migration step 0, re-measured on the coordinator build.
page_bytes_source: WebAssembly page size, equal to the dlmalloc 0.2.12 system granularity
isolate_bytes_source: Cloudflare Workers limits: "128 MB per isolate" (10^6 bytes, the smaller reading)
js_reserve_bytes_source: not measured for the probe (it measures glue only); the drill's model carries the measured JS reserve
glue_static_bytes_source: idle glue footprint 872 B (admitted build, 7 allocations) / 1,096 B (macro build), measured with one /stats request in flight (round2 run probe1 IDLE); stated margin: rounded up to the next power of two
glue_ticket_bytes_source: largest measured glue per entry over the six entry kinds, every export hand-written and each entry taking its own ticket (a Worker-to-Durable-Object request takes two): the largest per-invocation footprint ratio over 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 in flight (round2 run probe1, admitted build): fetch 272 B (240 B with a 4 KB URL: no URL dependence), Durable Object fetch 272 B (the 544-B Worker-to-DO chain minus the Worker's 272 B), alarm 248 B, queue 224 B, scheduled 192 B, waitUntil continuation 304 B. Stated margin: 304 B rounded up to the next power of two. The worker-macros exports measured 482 B (fetch), 979 B (fetch plus a DO hop under one entry), 480 B (alarm) and a 4 KB URL adding 3.5 KB
glue_resident_bytes_source: 24 B of glue footprint (one allocation) per co-resident Durable Object instance over 64 new instances, both builds (round2 run probe1 RESIDENT); the hand-written class holds a Resident token; stated margin: rounded up to the next power of two
min_route_bytes_source: the probe's per-route CONTROL footprint (every probe route)
largest_route_bytes_source: the probe's largest invocation (Worker fetch /wait): state page and CONTROL run (6 pages) + the handler future's block (1 page; the future is below 64 KiB) + the pages it lends its waitUntil continuation (child_bytes(0) + 1 page = 3 pages): 10 pages; witness: stats route_bound_exceeded stays 0 in the probe drive
stack_bytes_source: rustc 1.99.1 wasm32-unknown-unknown links the stack first with rust-lld's default -z stack-size=1048576: [__stack_low, __stack_high) = [0, 1,048,576) (scratch probe, 2026-10-31); the pool starts above static data, so the stack is outside every arena
stack_high_water_bytes_source: measured: the painted stack high-water of the instance that served every probe entry kind (fetch, Durable Object fetch and alarm, queue, scheduled, waitUntil), read from its postmortem after the trap test: 3,912 B (macro build), 3,848 B (admitted build), including the 256-B unpainted guard (round2 run probe1). Stated margin: half the linked stack, so the probe's clippy thresholds are stack_bytes / 2 - high-water
